findings.title: Architecture-scoped address-reviews emits have no legal path through the surface
findings.recommendation: The baseline orbit-address-reviews 'Architecture-scoped resolution logs' requirement mandates address-reviews-<TS>.json in orbit/architecture/.orbit-runs/ with change: null + doc, and the run-summary-emit delta routes ALL address-reviews emits through orbit emit. But the target-resolution contract classes commands into a single scope ('--doc to a change-scoped one ... is a clean usage error'; 'audit-drift is the one dual-scope command'), never naming address-reviews (or review) as change-or-doc capable per invocation, and the post-write class defines only 'the change status against a SYNTHETIC TRAIL' — undefined when there is no change. Name the architecture-capable command set explicitly (review, address-reviews, architect) with per-invocation flag-driven trail resolution, and define the doc-scoped address-reviews next_recommended composition (or explicitly carve that walk out of the surface).

findings.title: Clean architecture-mode review emit composes an invalid change-report pointer
findings.recommendation: The deterministic-facts rule (and orbit-review's persisted-summary delta, line 58) binds ALL review emits' clean-pass next_recommended to the 'orbit status --change <change> --report' render pointer and iteration to the report ordinal's counting rule — but for --as architecture, change is null, no report surface exists (the delta's own --render rule says so), and baseline iteration is anchored per doc, not per change trail. The iter-6 handoff-mirror fix covered architect emits only; state the architecture-mode review rule explicitly (e.g. mirror the payload's handoff.next_command like architect, and count iteration per doc), or scope the review clean-pointer rule to proposal/system.

findings.title: No task implements the orientation surfaced-skip-note behavior
findings.recommendation: The modified fault-isolation requirement makes spine-invalid exclusion SURFACED across bare, --full, and boot renders ('⚠ invalid emit skipped: <filename>') with a skipped_emits array in both JSON tiers — grep confirms none of this exists in src/core/orientation.ts today — yet group 4 covers only the boot render (4.1's 'degradation per orientation fault-isolation' reads as boot degrading under the policy, not implementing the policy's new surfacing). Add the bare/--full note + skipped_emits work and its tests to a task (4.1 extension or a 4.3).

findings.title: Boot mode-split enumerates architecture, which a change trail never holds
findings.recommendation: --boot reads the change's trail, and review-architecture emits persist to orbit/architecture/.orbit-runs/ — the '(proposal / system / architecture)' enumeration could send an implementer scanning the architecture trail for a change-scoped render. Drop 'architecture' from the split or note the mode cannot occur on a change trail.

findings.title: Design D8's 'no validation of the hint value' lags the gates delta's boundary check
findings.recommendation: The engine-gates delta (from the external-review fix) adds the rendering-boundary well-formedness check (single line, ≤80 chars, no control characters, malformed = inert); design D8 still says 'no validation of the hint value' flatly. Add 'beyond the rendering-boundary well-formedness check' so the design summary matches the normative delta.

findings.title: Post-sync the architect sweep is stated normatively in two requirements
findings.recommendation: The untouched baseline 'Architect authoring stance and capture' requirement already carries the R-d-8 residency sweep with its own 'Residency sweep before emit' scenario; the delta adds parallel sweep language + scenario to the emit requirement. Same substance, two homes — against the change's own one-home rule. Have the emit requirement cite the stance requirement (or fold the stance requirement's sweep sentence into this delta) rather than restating.

commentary: Strict validation and 25/25 fingerprints green; zero @review: residue; no baseline scenario dropped across all ten modified capabilities (the two renames are the deliberate verify-first retirement and the 6-to-7 spine bump). The change is notably self-compliant: its own tasks.md preamble parses under the grammar it specifies, its explore.md practices the standing-recommendation format it mandates, and the frozen record vocabulary is used consistently everywhere including the archive-consistency surfaces. What looseness remains clusters at one seam — architecture-scoped emits for commands other than architect. The iter-6 walk answered the authorship question for architect via the handoff mirror, but the identical question recurs one command over (review --as architecture's clean pointer, doc-scoped address-reviews), suggesting the fix was applied at the finding's literal anchor rather than across the seam's family. The other genuine hole is task-coverage: the orientation fail-loud surfacing is fully specified but invisible from tasks.md, the one artifact the apply phase actually executes from. Engine claims were spot-verified against source throughout and held every time.
